name: Willamette Valley

climate: Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris and Chardonnay sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Most rain falls in winter. Dry summers keep mildew and rot down, though young vines may need watering.

keyfacts: Willamette Valley is Oregon's largest AVA, established in 1983, and has a cool, moist climate recognized worldwide for Pinot Noir.
Most producers do not irrigate, which supports deep-rooted vines and rapid ripening from some water stress.
Most vineyards sit on southeast-facing slopes, and soils are generally marine sedimentary, volcanic and loess.
Winters are cool and wet and summers dry and warm, with heat above 90°F on only 5 to 15 days per year.
Yamhill-Carlton District and McMinnville only allow vineyards between 200 and 1,000 feet in elevation to use the appellation name.

blurb.text: Oregon's largest AVA, covering the Willamette River basin, with a cool, moist climate and worldwide recognition for Pinot Noir. Pinot Noir is 72 percent of plantings, then Pinot Gris. Eyrie Vineyard's showing at the 1979 Wine Olympics first brought it attention.
